𝕏 Follow me on X • 🤗 Hugging Face • 💻 Blog • 📙 LLM Engineer's Handbook


The LLM course is divided into three parts: 1. 🧩 **LLM Fundamentals** is optional and covers fundamental knowledge about mathematics, Python, and neural networks. 2. 🧑‍🔬 **The LLM Scientist** focuses on building the best possible LLMs using the latest techniques. 3. 👷 **The LLM Engineer** focuses on creating LLM-based applications and deploying them. > [!NOTE] > Based on this course, I co-wrote the [LLM Engineer's Handbook](https://packt.link/a/9781836200079), a hands-on book that covers an end-to-end LLM application from design to deployment. The LLM course will always stay free, but you can support my work by purchasing this book. For a more comprehensive version of this course, check out the [DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/mlabonne/llm-course/). ## 📝 Notebooks A list of notebooks and articles I wrote about LLMs.
Toggle section (optional) ### Tools | Notebook | Description | Notebook | |----------|-------------|----------| | 🧐 [LLM AutoEval](https://github.com/mlabonne/llm-autoeval) | Automatically evaluate your LLMs using RunPod | | | 🥱 LazyMergekit | Easily merge models using MergeKit in one click. | | | 🦎 LazyAxolotl | Fine-tune models in the cloud using Axolotl in one click. | | | ⚡ AutoQuant | Quantize LLMs in GGUF, GPTQ, EXL2, AWQ, and HQQ formats in one click. | | | 🌳 Model Family Tree | Visualize the family tree of merged models. | | | 🚀 ZeroSpace | Automatically create a Gradio chat interface using a free ZeroGPU. | | | ✂️ AutoAbliteration | Automatically abliteration models with custom datasets. | | | 🧼 AutoDedup | Automatically deduplicate datasets using the Rensa library. | | ### Fine-tuning | Notebook | Description | Article | Notebook | |---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Fine-tune Llama 3.1 with Unsloth | Ultra-efficient supervised fine-tuning in Google Colab. | [Article](https://mlabonne.github.io/blog/posts/2024-07-29_Finetune_Llama31.html) |

> **The only places to get a genuine License code for the supporter models are [Buy Me a Coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/kruk2), [Unifans](https://app.unifans.io/c/kruk2), and for China the seller in the [Chinese README](README.zh.md#在闲鱼购买).** > > **支持者模型的正版许可证码只能通过 [Buy Me a Coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/kruk2)、[Unifans](https://app.unifans.io/c/kruk2) 或 [闲鱼](README.zh.md#在闲鱼购买) 获取。** [**English**](README.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [中文](README.zh.md) # Jasna Jasna restores mosaics in videos and images. It is free, has a simple app and a command line, and runs on your GPU. ## Contents **Start here** - [What Jasna does](#what-jasna-does) - [What you need](#what-you-need) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Help and community](#help-and-community) - [Supporting the project](#supporting-the-project) (supporter models) **Advanced** - [How Jasna works](#how-jasna-works) - [Command line](#command-line) - [All guides](#all-guides) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Licensing](#licensing) - [Acknowledgments](#acknowledgments) ## What Jasna does - Finds mosaics in a video and restores them. The rest of the picture is not touched. - Two restoration models: fast **BasicVSR++** (free) and slow but more detailed **LTX** (for supporters, NVIDIA only). - Restores only the parts you choose, with a preview, in the **Segment Editor**. - Works with VR180 videos and still images (SD 1.5, for supporters). - Lets you watch a video restored live in the **Video Player**, without making a file. ## What you need - **NVIDIA** GTX 16-series / RTX 20-series or newer, with a recent driver (610+ on Windows, 580+ on Linux). GTX 10-series and older don't work. - Or **AMD** Radeon RX 7000/9000 (experimental). - A folder on a local disk, with no Chinese, Japanese, accented or other non-English characters in its path.
More details - NVIDIA: your GPU needs compute capability 7.5 or higher in NVIDIA's [GPU table](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda/gpus). - AMD: a GPU supported by ROCm (Radeon RX 7000/9000, Radeon 780M/760M/740M, Ryzen AI). On Windows, AMD Adrenalin driver 26.8.1 or newer. Secondary restoration and LTX are NVIDIA only. - Disk format: NTFS on Windows; ext4, Btrfs, XFS or ZFS on Linux. Network disks are not supported. Use an SSD; on a hard disk (HDD) Jasna starts and loads models slowly. - LTX needs an NVIDIA RTX GPU, at least 8 GB VRAM and 16 GB RAM. See [What LTX needs](docs/en/models.md#what-ltx-needs).
## Quick start 1. Download the release for your system and GPU. 2. Unpack it into a folder with no Chinese, Japanese, accented or other non-English characters in the path. 3. Start the app: - Windows: double-click `jasna.exe`. - Linux NVIDIA: run the `jasna` file. - Linux AMD: run `run_jasna_amd.sh`. 4. Add a video, choose settings and click the **▶** button at the bottom. **Your first job is slow.** On NVIDIA, Jasna first prepares the models for your exact GPU. This takes about **15–60 minutes**, only once. Close other apps and don't use the PC during this time. When you update Jasna, copy the `model_weights` folder to the new version, so you don't wait again. Every setting has a tooltip: move the mouse over the ⓘ icon. Out of GPU memory (VRAM)? Lower **Max Clip Size**, for example from `90` to `60`. See [Tuning](docs/en/tuning.md). ## Help and community - [App guide](docs/en/gui.md): the queue, presets, output names, the Video Player and activation. - [SLS Discord](https://discord.gg/FgrSuwZS3s): examples, help and settings. Jasna has a [new channel](https://discord.com/channels/1196376491815092265/1556960822578909244); older posts stay in the [old channel (archived)](https://discord.com/channels/1196376491815092265/11990
